Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y={x}^{2}$ and lines $y=7x,$ $y=x+12,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
question.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/ee6fd6a0b89a879d5803a98fda7e80a93926566995bea5f47a05aa7ab2986375.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 7x\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+12\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{7x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+12}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$
